angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 425,768 km at 135.30 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 7.3912 +/- 0.0180 mas (same row, RUWE 1.05): 135.30 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.612 +/- 0.013 solar radii from Kanodia et al. 2021, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-532 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....162..135K/abstract): 425,768 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.639 +/- 0.023 solar masses from Kanodia et al. 2021, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-532 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....162..135K/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3927 +/- 37 K from Kanodia et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-532 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....162..135K/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Kanodia et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-532 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....162..135K/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-532.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.670, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
